The Savonius wind turbine is a type of vertical axis wind turbine (VAWT) that is propelled by drag.
The Savonius wind turbine was invented by Sigurd J. Savonius in 1922 and first commercialized in the 1920s.

The study used three different Savonius rotor models with varying blade sizes: Model 1 (height 1 m, diameter 0.4 m), Model 2 (height 0.75 m, diameter 0.3 m), and Model 3 (height 0.5 m, diameter 0.2 m).
The simulations were performed using ANSYS Fluent 2021 R21 with a constant upstream wind speed of 9.2 m/s.
The power coefficient (Cp) of all models increased with tip-speed ratio (TSR) and reached the highest efficiency at a TSR of around 0.9.
Model 2 had the highest power coefficient, followed by Model 3 and Model 1.
The maximum power output was 24.13 Watts, achieved by Model 3.
The torque and torque coefficient were higher at low TSR and decreased as the TSR increased.
Compared to the peak power coefficient, Model 2 was 31.99% higher than Model 3 and 65.63% higher than Model 1.
The Savonius wind turbine design has the advantages of being able to capture wind from any direction and rotating slowly, with a strong starting torque and no wind direction issues.
The study aimed to maximize wind energy harvesting and rotational mechanical electric generation of Savonius rotors by varying the rotor blade size and observing the performance.
The blade size significantly impacts the efficiency of Savonius wind turbines, and the proper selection of blade size is crucial for efficient operation.
The study used computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis to evaluate the aerodynamic characteristics of the Savonius rotor wind turbines.
The simulation was carried out using a transient time flow with a constant upstream wind speed.
The SIMPLE algorithm was used for the pressure-velocity coupling scheme in the solution method.
